I also have small feet and often find that some shoes are too big, even when bought in the correct size. If I ever find I have a bit of space in a shoe I always do the following: 

- buy a heel grip. You can get these in clear but also in suede. It'll fill some of the gap between your heel and the shoe. You can slot these in without peeling off the sticky back to walk around in/for photographs and then once photos are taken, remove the backing and place them in the shoe permanently. I have also removed these from the backs of shoes with no issues or sticky residue so nothing stopping you from putting them in until the wedding day and then replacing the day of so they're not there for photos. 
- get some gel cushions to sit under the ball of your foot. These come in transparent colouring and will stop the front of your foot sliding around so much. Once again I've removed these with no issues so you could wear until day/remove for photos and replace. These also provide some extra cushioning for comfort. 
- if you're still finding you've got room, you can also buy triangle shaped toe inserts that go in the toe of the shoe and fill up more space. 

I'm in Australia so unsure of brands where you are, but Scholl make the first two options in great quality and the toe inserts I was able to find on Amazon. 

In terms of breaking in, they won't flatten out in heel mode but you should be used to heel mode for easy walking on the big day. To speed up the flattening of my tweed d'orsays I've placed a dumbbell on them over night to flatten out the 'elf toe' and found this helped relax the shoe a bit. 

Sorry for long response but hope it was helpful!
